meta.title: When is the last mow of the year in Michigan? | Grand Scapes
meta.description: Keep mowing while the grass grows, then drop one notch, about half an inch, for the last cut. What MSU Extension says about timing, height and the leaves.

title: The last mow of the year **in Michigan.**
lede: In Michigan, the last mow comes after the leaves are handled and the grass has stopped growing, late in the fall. MSU Extension's advice is simple: keep mowing as long as the grass grows, then lower the mower one notch, about half an inch, for a final clean up cut.
short: Keep mowing as long as the grass is growing. There is no set date on the calendar.
MSU Extension says once leaf mulching is done and top growth has essentially stopped, it is OK to lower the height for the last cut.
Drop it no more than one notch on the mower, typically half an inch, MSU says. Do not scalp it.
The point is to clean up leftover leaf bits and keep the grass from going into winter too tall.
Never take off more than a third of the blade in one cut, in fall or any other time.

sections.h: When to make the last cut
p: There is no fixed date for the last mow in Michigan. It depends on when the grass stops growing. As long as it keeps growing, it keeps needing a cut, and a lawn left alone through a warm, wet fall can go into winter shaggy.

MSU Extension puts the timing this way: once you are past the leaf mulching period and the turf has essentially stopped its top growth, it is OK to lower the height and give it a final trim. In practice, that is after the last big leaf drop, when a week goes by and the lawn barely needs cutting.

Not much lower. MSU Extension recommends lowering the mowing height no more than one notch on your mower, which is typically half an inch. If you mowed at 3.5 inches all summer, the last cut lands around 3. If you mowed at 3, it lands around 2.5.

Scalping the lawn down for winter is an old habit, and it is not what MSU recommends. Its homeowner mowing bulletin says mowing too short reduces the grass plant's ability to make food, and that lowering the height reduces the root system.

table.note: MSU Extension's range for Michigan home lawns is 2 to 3.75 inches. A notch on your mower may be a little more or less than half an inch, so check your deck.

p: MSU gives two reasons for that last, slightly lower cut. It cleans up leftover leaf mulch and debris, and it keeps the turf from being too tall going into winter.

Late fall mowing and leaves go together. MSU's mowing bulletin describes studies that mowed up to 6 inches of tree leaves into lawns with no adverse effects, and its fall advice is to raise the mower for leaves and not let them pile up past three to four inches.

Whole leaves left on the lawn are the real winter risk. MSU's Smart Gardening tip sheet warns that leaves piled up under wet, heavy snow can mean disaster for the grass below. So the order is leaves first, then the final cut. For the leaf side, see our note on whether to [mulch leaves or remove them](/journal/leaves-mulch-them-or-remove-them/).

list: **Wait for the grass to stop.** If it is still growing every week, it is not the last mow yet.
**Finish the leaves.** Mulch them in or haul them off before the final cut, so nothing sits on the lawn under the snow.
**Drop one notch.** About half an inch, per MSU. Not lower.
**Mow dry grass with a sharp blade.** MSU says a dull blade tears grass and leaves a frayed, brownish look.
**Take a third or less.** MSU's rule of thumb is to never remove more than a third of the leaf surface at once. If the lawn got away from you, bring it down over two cuts.

sections.h: How our late season cuts go
p: On our [weekly lawn mowing](/lawn-mowing/) route, the late cuts change with the weather. Some weeks are mostly grass and some are mostly leaves, and some of the last cuts are done with a bagger on the mower, which picks up chopped leaves along with the clippings. Heavy leaf drops go to our [fall cleanup and leaf removal](/fall-cleanup-and-leaf-removal/), where the leaf vacuum hauls them off.
If you have a question about your lawn's last cut of the year, [text Rob](sms:+18109903040).
